subject: Prod inference parity: tool-calling, streaming & structured-output next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 15:14:00 -0700
Subject: Prod inference parity: tool-calling, streaming & structured-output next steps

Hi Elena / Tom —

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for walking us through the Nova Products use cases. Below is a short recap plus a concrete test plan we think will surface the parity gaps quickly. I’ve attached a one-page matrix summarizing differences we discussed and the demo recording.

Quick recap of needs you called out:
- Low-latency streaming for live assistants (partial tokens visible to user)
- Deterministic structured outputs for ingestion (JSON schema enforcement)
- Tool/function calling for invoking internal APIs (auth + webhook flow)
- Competitive parity vs AWS Bedrock & Google Vertex for cost/perf and for enterprise compliance

Proposed next tests (20–40h of effort total):
1) Streaming behavior: a 1000-request run with short (avg 40 token) responses to compare time-to-first-byte and chunking.
2) Function / tool-calling: 50 flows invoking an external webhook (auth token rotation) to verify deterministic argument shapes and error modes.
3) Structured output parity: run our sample eval harness with your JSON schemas (see Drive link) and measure validation/pass rates.
4) End-to-end latency & cost: tokenized throughput test with redwood-medium and large, and a matched run on Bedrock/Vertex if you can provide creds.

Immediate asks for you to unblock tests:
- Confirm which hyperscaler endpoints you want us to prioritize (AWS Bedrock, Vertex, both).
- Share the minimal JSON schemas for ingestion (or confirm we should reuse the sheet in Drive).
- Let us know who from infra can provide short-lived creds for the hyperscaler runs (we’ll provide exact instructions).

Timeline (tentative):
- Aug 10: test harness + sample prompts delivered to your team
- Aug 11–14: you run tests / we run hosted runs in parallel
- Aug 17: quick sync to review results and next steps

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.pdf, demo-recording-20260802.mp4

If that all looks good I’ll kick off the harness repo and drop the curl examples and a minimal test account for you to use.

Best,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Prod inference parity: tool-calling, streaming & structured-output next steps

Hi Elena — quick technical plan and samples below (pulled from the parity-harness we’ll share).

Streaming notes:
- Redwood streaming is SSE-like with chunked JSON deltas. We flush on token boundaries and on punctuation heuristics to minimize perceived latency. Time-to-first-byte typically < 80ms for short responses on our hosted tier; we’ll capture tail latency in the harness.
- Example client behavior: handle partial JSON fragments and reassemble on the client. We include sequence ids and chunk_offsets in each event to make reassembly deterministic.

Function / tool-calling semantics:
- We support an explicit function schema in the request. On match, the model returns a structured call object: {"name":"<tool>", "args": { ... }}.
- Redwood offers guaranteed JSON quoting + schema validation hooks: we run a lightweight validator before emitting the call to your webhook. If validation fails we return a structured error object and can optionally attempt a single auto-correction pass.
- Retries: we recommend idempotent webhook endpoints. Our sample harness demonstrates exponential backoff (retry after 500ms, 1s, 2s) and a dead-letter queue for persistent failures.

Test harness (what we’ll provide):
1) Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/parity-test-harness — includes a Dockerized consumer that mimics your webhook and an SSE client for streaming tests.
2) Commands (example):
   - Stream test: curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <test-token>" \n     "https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream?model=redwood-medium" \n     -d '{"prompt":"<sample>","stream":true}'
   - Function call sample (expected payload to webhook):
     POST /webhook  HTTP/1.1
     Host: webhook.nova.internal
     Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>
     Content-Type: application/json

     {
       "call_id": "abc-123",
       "tool": "inventory_lookup",
       "args": {"sku":"SKU-100"},
       "metadata": {"model":"redwood-large","request_ts":"2026-08-03T20:43:00Z"}
     }

Latency & tokenization guidance:
- Tokenization: we’ll include the tokenizer mapping tool in the harness so you can compare token counts across Bedrock/Vertex.
- Measurement: measure time-to-first-byte, median per-token latency, and 95th/99th tail. We’ll provide a benchmarking script.

Next steps from our side: we’ll push the harness and an example test account (read-only test key) by Tue EOD. If you can upload the schemas and grant a short-lived Bedrock/Vertex role, we’ll queue those comparative runs.

— Rishi
